profile.research_note:
Current operator of this cable landing station following the 2020 T-Mobile merger and 2023-2024 Cogent wireline sale is unresolved; retained under Sprint per no-reassignment-without-confirmation policy.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is the Manasquan Cable Landing Station in Manasquan, New Jersey, terminating the TAT-14 transatlantic fiber optic cable system, a consortium cable that entered service in 2001 connecting the United States to the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Denmark, and the Netherlands. Sprint Corporation, a Kansas based wireless and wireline carrier, was one of the original TAT-14 consortium members alongside carriers including AT&T, Verizon, France Telecom, and Deutsche Telekom, each historically responsible for landing and operating a segment of the shared cable system. Sprint merged into T-Mobile US on April 1, 2020. Following that merger, T-Mobile sold the bulk of its legacy wireline business, including more than thirty former Sprint network switch sites converted to colocation space, to Cogent Communications in a deal announced May 2023 and closed 2024, structured as a one dollar sale with revenue sharing terms. No source found in this research confirms whether this Manasquan landing station specifically was included in that Cogent transaction, since cable landing stations tied to multi carrier consortium cables are often governed separately from ordinary switch and colocation real estate; current operational control of this facility is not published and is treated as unresolved. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project and is reused here for the facility record.
Current operator of the specific Manasquan TAT-14 landing station post-merger is not confirmed; not established whether it was part of the Cogent wireline deal.

reading: Sprint Corporation was a Kansas based wireless and wireline telecommunications carrier that merged into T-Mobile US on April 1, 2020, forming the New T-Mobile. The single Sprint linked facility in this registry, the Manasquan Cable Landing Station in Manasquan, New Jersey, terminates the TAT-14 transatlantic fiber optic cable system, a consortium cable that entered service in 2001 connecting the United States to the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Denmark, and the Netherlands. Sprint was one of the original TAT-14 consortium members alongside carriers including AT&T, Verizon, France Telecom, and Deutsche Telekom, each historically responsible for landing and operating a segment of the shared cable system. Following the T-Mobile merger, T-Mobile sold the bulk of its legacy wireline business, including more than thirty former Sprint network switch sites converted to colocation space, to Cogent Communications in a deal announced in May 2023 and closed in 2024, structured as a one dollar sale with revenue sharing terms. No source found in this research specifically confirms whether the Manasquan TAT-14 landing station was included in the Cogent transaction, since cable landing stations tied to multi carrier consortium cables are often governed separately from ordinary switch and colocation real estate. Current day to day operational control of the Manasquan facility is not published and should be treated as unresolved pending facility level research. This record is retained under the Sprint name per registry policy against deleting historical operator entries, with the T-Mobile merger and Cogent transaction noted here for context.
